Rashi on Chullin 60b:10:1.hebrew: שעיוו את מקומן - יצאו משם ונתעוות, שחרב:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:10:1.english: Because they ruined their place - They departed from there and it became ruined, [meaning] that it was destroyed:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:10:2.hebrew: עוית - רתת וחלחלה, בלע"ז קרנפ"א:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:10:2.english: Convulsions [avit] - Trembling and shuddering; in Old French: crampe [cramp/spasm]:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:10:3.english: Sixteen darei shinei [rows of teeth] - Rows of teeth:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:11:1.hebrew: הרבה מקראות - יש שדומה לקוראיהן שהן ראוין לישרף, שלא היה לו לכותבם, שאין להם צורך בתורה, וגנאי הוא לחברן עם הקדושה:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:11:1.english: Many verses - There are [verses] that seem to their readers as though they are fit to be burned, [for they think] that He should not have written them, since there is no need for them in the Torah, and it is a disgrace to join them with the sacred [writings]:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:11:2.english: And they are the essence of Torah - Great reasons depend upon them. And now [the Gemara] proceeds to enumerate them until the end of the discussion:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:11:3.english: Hazerim as far as Gaza - [This area is part of] the Land of Israel:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:11:4.hebrew: מאי נפקא לן מינה - אי לאו מקומן של אלו היה, אלא מקום אחרים, ואלו גרשום:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:11:4.english: What [practical] difference does this make for us - [what does it matter] if it was not the place of these [the Caphtorim], but rather the place of others [the Avvim], and these [the Caphtorim] expelled them?

Rashi on Chullin 60b:12:1.english: Nor with my son, nor with my grandson - And the generations [of the oath] had not yet passed:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:12:2.english: Caphtorim - They are not from the Philistines:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:12:3.hebrew: ליתו וליפקו - ארעא מפלשתים, וליתו ישראל וליפקו מינייהו. וקסבר ריש לקיש עוים מפלשתים היו, ולמאן דאמר מתימן היו, להך מילתא נמי אצטריך: משום דאזהרינהו שלא להתגרות בבני עשו, אמר רחמנא ליתו כפתורים וליפקו מעוים וניתו ישראל וניפקו מינייהו. ושאר מקראות הדומין לזה באלה הדברים, כגון "ובשעיר ישבו החורים", ובמואבים ובעמונים כתיב "רפאים ישבו בה", כולהו טעמא אית בהו: דבכולהו כתיב "ארץ רפאים תחשב", לפי שנאמר לאברהם אבינו בין הבתרים "לזרעך נתתי וגו'", וקחשיב "ואת הרפאים". וכשיצאו ממצרים ועברו דרך הר שעיר ועמון ומואב, שנקראו כבר "ארץ רפאים", היה עולה על דעתם להתגרות בהם, כסבורים זו היא שניתנה לאברהם. ומנעם הקדוש ברוך הוא ואמר להם: "ארץ רפאים" ודאי נחשבת, שהרפאים ישבו בה מקדם, אבל לא זו היא שנתתי לאברהם, אלא לאלו נתתיה שגרשום משם וישבו תחתיהם — בשכר אברהם, שיצאו בני עשו הימנו, ולוט היה קרוב לאברהם. וכשהגיעו לחבל ארגוב, כתיב (דברים ג) "ההוא יקרא ארץ רפאים" — זו היא שנתתי לאביכם:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:12:3.english: Let them come and remove - [the] land from [the] Philistines, and let Israel come and take [it] from them. And Reish Lakish holds [that the] Avvim were from [the] Philistines; and according to the one who says they were from Teman, for this matter too it was necessary: because He warned them not to provoke [war with] the children of Esau, the Merciful One said, "Let the Caphtorim come and remove [the land] from the Avvim, and let Israel come and take [it] from them." And [regarding] the other verses similar to this in [the book of] Deuteronomy — such as "and in Seir the Horites dwelt," and regarding the Moabites and the Ammonites it is written, "Rephaim dwelt there" — all of them have a reason: for in all of them it is written, "It is accounted a land of Rephaim," because it was said to Abraham our forefather between the pieces, "To your descendants I have given [this land], etc.," and it enumerates "and the Rephaim." And when they went out of Egypt and passed by way of Mount Seir, Ammon, and Moab, which were already called "a land of Rephaim," it entered their minds to provoke [war with] them, thinking, "This is the [land] that was given to Abraham." And the Holy One, Blessed be He, prevented them and said to them: "It is certainly accounted a 'land of Rephaim,' for the Rephaim dwelt there of old; however, this is not the one that I gave to Abraham, rather I gave it to these [nations] who drove them out from there and dwelt in their stead — as a reward for Abraham, since the children of Esau descended from him, and Lot was a relative of Abraham." And when they reached the region of Argob, it is written (Deuteronomy 3), "That shall be called a land of Rephaim" — this is the [land] that I gave to your forefather:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:13:1.hebrew: והוא נלחם במלך מואב - למה לו לאשמועינן? אלא משום דכתיב "אל תצר את מואב" וגו':
Rashi on Chullin 60b:13:1.english: Who had fought against the king of Moab - Why did [Scripture] need to inform us [of this]? Rather, [it is] because it is written, “Be not at enmity with Moab” (Deuteronomy 2:9), etc.

Rashi on Chullin 60b:13:2.english: And this is what Rav Pappa says - in tractate Gittin (38a):

Rashi on Chullin 60b:13:3.hebrew: עמון ומואב טהרו בסיחון - ע"י סיחון טהרו ארצם לישראל: במואב כתיב (במדבר כא) "והוא נלחם וגו'". ובעמון מפורש בנחלת בני גד בספר יהושע (יג): "ויהי להם הגבול יעזר וכל ארץ הגלעד וחצי ארץ בני עמון", וקא חשיב ואזיל, וכתיב בסיפיה: "יתר ממלכות סיחון" — אלמא סיחון כבש לארץ בני עמון. ועוד מצינו במלך בני עמון שאמר למלאכי יפתח: "כי לקח ישראל את ארצי מארנון ועד היבוק" — אלמא ארץ בני עמון הוא, והם מסיחון כבשוה, דכתיב בו: "וירשו את ארצו מארנון ועד היבוק", אבל מהנשאר בידם לא לקחו כלום:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:13:3.english: Ammon and Moab were purified by Sihon - Through Sihon, their land was purified [i.e., rendered permitted] for Israel. Regarding Moab, it is written (Numbers 21[:26]): "who had fought [against the former king of Moab], etc." And regarding Ammon, it is stated explicitly in [the description of] the inheritance of the children of Gad in the Book of Joshua (13[:25, 27]): "And their border was Jazer, and all the land of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon," and [the verse] continues enumerating, and at the end of it, it is written: "the rest of the kingdom of Sihon" — thus, Sihon had conquered the land of the children of Ammon. Furthermore, we find regarding the king of the children of Ammon, who said to the messengers of Jephthah [Judges 11:13]: "Because Israel took my land from the Arnon to the Jabbok" — thus, it was the land of the children of Ammon, and they [Israel] conquered it from Sihon, as it is written concerning him [Numbers 21:24]: "and they possessed his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok"; however, from what remained in their [Ammon's] hands, they took nothing:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:14:1.english: The Sidonians call, etc. - Why is [this verse] needed:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:14:2.hebrew: תנא שניר ושריון הרי ארץ ישראל הן - וחרמון קרוב לצידונים ולאמורי, ובנו עליו כרכים — זה קרא לו שריון, וזה קרא לו שניר:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:14:2.english: [A Sage] taught: Senir and Sirion are mountains of the Land of Israel - and Hermon is near the Sidonians and the Amorites, and they built cities upon it — this one called it Sirion, and that one called it Senir:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:15:1.english: He removed them city by city - What does [the verse] teach us?

Rashi on Chullin 60b:15:2.hebrew: כי היכי דלא ליקרו - מצרים לאחיו לאחר זמן "גולים בני גולים", לכך הגלם:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:15:2.english: So that they would not call - [Meaning, so that the] Egyptians [would not call] his brothers, after some time, "exiles, sons of exiles"; therefore he [Joseph] exiled them:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:1:1.hebrew: לר' חנינא בר פפא - דאמר מדעתן יצאו דשאים למיניהם, ולא נצטוו על כך:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:1:1.english: According to Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa - who said [that] the grasses came forth of their own accord after their kinds, and were not commanded concerning this:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:1:2.english: What is [the halakha] - to graft one onto the other:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:1:3.english: With them [ideihu] - The Holy One, blessed be He, agreed with them:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:2:1.hebrew: כתיב הגדולים - דמשמע שניהם גדולים, וכתיב הקטן:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:2:1.english: It is written: “the great [lights]” - which implies [that] both of them [were] great, and [yet] it is written: “the lesser [light]”:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:3:1.english: Go and rule during the day and during the night - [This] is a consolation:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:3:2.english: A candle at noon - a candle at midday does not give light:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:3:3.english: The day - [This refers to] the sun:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:3:4.hebrew: תקופות - נמנין לחמה, ועל התקופה מעברין את השנה, בסנהדרין (דף יא:):
Rashi on Chullin 60b:3:4.english: Seasons [tekufot] - are counted by the sun, and based on the season they intercalate the year, [as taught] in Sanhedrin (11b):

Rashi on Chullin 60b:3:5.hebrew: יעקב הקטן - "מי יקום יעקב כי קטן הוא" (עמוס ז):
Rashi on Chullin 60b:3:5.english: Jacob the small - [As the verse states:] "How shall Jacob stand? For he is small" (Amos 7[:2]):

Rashi on Chullin 60b:3:6.english: David, the youngest - [This] is a verse in Samuel (I 17):

Rashi on Chullin 60b:4:1.hebrew: בכולהו רגלים כתיב (במדבר כח) "ושעיר חטאת אחד", ולא כתיב בהו "לה'":
Rashi on Chullin 60b:4:1.english: For all the festivals, it is written (Numbers 28), "and one goat [for] a sin offering," and "for the Lord" is not written regarding them:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:5:1.english: [It] was not yet in the earth - It was not yet in the earth:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:5:2.hebrew: ועמדו על פתח קרקע - מתאוים למי גשמים, כדכתיב (בראשית ב) "כי לא המטיר", עד שנברא אדם בששי:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:5:2.english: And they stood at the opening of the ground - longing for rainwater, as it is written (Genesis 2[:5]), "For [the Lord God] had not caused it to rain," until Adam was created on the sixth [day]:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:6:2.hebrew: היינו דרב אסי - שהקדוש ב"ה מתאוה לתפלתן של צדיקים:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:6:2.english: This is [the statement] of Rav Asi - that the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires the prayers of the righteous:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:7:1.hebrew: שיש לה שני גבין - ולכך נקראת שסועה, תאומה:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:7:1.english: Which has two backs - And therefore it is called shesu'ah, [meaning] twinned:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:7:2.english: But was Moses our teacher a kenigi [hunter] - [meaning,] one who hunts animals in the hunt:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:7:3.hebrew: או בליסטרי - מורה בקשת לחיות, ובלע"ז בלישטדי"ר. ומנין היה בקי בחיות הללו, שאין אדם בקי בהם:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:7:3.english: Or was he an archer - One who shoots with a bow at animals, and in Old French, balistedor [crossbowman]. And from where was [Moses] familiar with these animals, with which no person is familiar?

Rashi on Chullin 60b:8:1.hebrew: כתוב קניגי ובליסטרי - אגדה זה כתוב, שיש בה תיבות יפין ולשון צח:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:8:1.english: Write kinnigi and ballisteri - Write this aggada, as it contains beautiful words and eloquent language:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:8:2.hebrew: ופרשה - מאי קניגי ובליסטרי באגדתיך. ומשום דנקט "כתוב באגדתיך", נקט נמי להאי קרא דסרני פלשתים:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:8:2.english: And explain it - [meaning, explain] what kinnigi and ballisteri are in your [book of] aggada. And because [the Gemara] mentioned "write [it] in your [book of] aggada," it also cites this verse of the lords of the Philistines:

Rashi on Chullin 60b:9:2.hebrew: מתימן - בן אליפז בן עשו באו, ואיוו לאלהי פלשתים, ויצאו ממקומם ובאו לגור ביניהם, ולהכי לא חשיב ששה סרני פלשתים:
Rashi on Chullin 60b:9:2.english: From Teiman - [who was] the son of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, they came, and they desired the gods of the Philistines, and they left their place and came to dwell among them, and therefore [the verse] does not count six lords of the Philistines:

Tosafot on Chullin 60b:2:1.hebrew: אמרה ירח - בלשון תורה לשון זכר הוא, דכתיב (יהושע י פי"ג): "וירח עמד":
Tosafot on Chullin 60b:2:1.english: The moon said [feminine] - In the language of the Torah [Scripture], ["moon"] is masculine, as it is written (Joshua 10:13): "and the moon stood still [masculine]":

Tosafot on Chullin 60b:7:1.hebrew: וכי משה קניגי היה או בליסטרי היה - שהיה יודע להכיר השסועה. וא"ת: והא אמרינן בהמפלת (נדה כד.) דשסועה באה מבהמה טהורה, וליכא מאן דפליג, ואם כן יכול להיות שבהמה טהורה היה לו למשה וילדה לו שסועה, ולא אצטריך למהוי קניגי? וי"ל: דשמא שסועה אינה באה אלא מבהמה שאינה מצויה בינינו:
Tosafot on Chullin 60b:7:1.english: But was Moses a hunter, or was he an archer - [meaning] that he knew how to recognize the shesua. And if you say: But do we not say in [the chapter entitled] Hamapelet (Niddah 24a) that a shesua comes from a kosher animal, and there is no one who disagrees — and if so, it could be that Moses had a kosher animal and it gave birth to a shesua for him, and he did not need to be a hunter? One can answer: Perhaps a shesua comes only from an animal that is not common among us:

Tosafot on Chullin 60b:9:1.hebrew: עוים מתימן באו כו' - ב' מקראות הם בספר יהושע (יג), והכי כתיב: "חמשת סרני פלשתים העזתי והאשדודי האשקלוני הגתי והעקרוני והעוים", והדר כתיב: "מתימן כל ארץ הכנעני ומערה אשר לצידונים עד אפקה עד גבול האמורי". והשתא מפרשה רב: והעוים דכתיב בסוף קרא קמא, קאי אתימן דבראש קרא דבתריה:
Tosafot on Chullin 60b:9:1.english: The Avvim came from Teiman, etc. - There are two verses in the Book of Joshua (13), and thus it is written: "The five lords of the Philistines: the Gazite, and the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite, and the Ekronite, also the Avvim," and then it is written: "from Teiman, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, unto Aphek, to the border of the Amorites." And now Rav explains it: "also the Avvim," which is written at the end of the first verse, refers to "from Teiman," which is at the beginning of the following verse:
